Telomeres are caps found at the end of each chromosome. Every time a cell divides, its telomeres shorten.
Eventually, the telomeres become so short that a cell will no longer be able to undergo mitosis, and cell death occurs.

The theory of evolution by natural selection is a well-supported, widely accepted explanation of how life has and continues to change over time. In a nutshell, there is a struggle for survival, and individuals with desirable traits are more likely to survive and reproduce, therefore passing on their traits to their offspring.
